title: Focal Length of a Convex Lens
subject: physics
aim: To find the focal length of a convex lens by plotting 1/v against 1/u.
theory:
The thin lens formula (Cartesian sign convention) is

$$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$$

For a real object, $u$ is negative. Using distances $|u|$ and $v$, this becomes $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{|u|} = \frac{1}{f}$, so a graph of $1/v$ against $1/|u|$ is a straight line meeting both axes at $1/f$.
procedure: Place the object beyond the focal length of the lens.
Move the image needle until there is no parallax with the image.
Record the object distance |u| and image distance v.
Repeat for at least five object positions.
Plot 1/v against 1/|u| and find f from the intercepts.
precautions: Keep the tips of the needles and the lens centre at the same height.

viva.question: What is the power of a lens?
viva.answer: P = 1/f with f in metres; the unit is the dioptre.

viva.question: Where must the object be for a real, same-size image?
What is parallax?
viva.answer: The apparent relative shift of two objects when the eye moves; it vanishes when they coincide.
